bae2026chromium: The chromium plating process is subject to an environmental constraint: analysing the CrO3 concentration in the bath takes a lead time of more than 24 hours. On site this has meant dosing chemicals on the basis of an operator's experience, a leading cause of process deviation and quality variation. To overcome that limitation, this study introduces a weekly time-series forecasting model and proposes moving from the existing intuitive approach to a data-driven, anticipatory decision-making scheme. Concentration data accumulated from 2022 to 2024 was used as the training period, and forecasting performance was evaluated against 26 weeks of measured data from the first half of 2025. The experiments used the traditional models ARIMA, Holt-Winters and Prophet together with the recent time-series foundation models TimesFM and Chronos. ARIMA and Holt-Winters were the more accurate on Tank 3, whose trend is stable, but TimesFM demonstrated the best forecasting performance and operational stability on the more volatile Tank 5 and in the overall combined evaluation. In particular, by quantitatively analysing the error characteristics near the boundaries of the actual control specification (234-255 g/L), the study confirms that the proposed forecasting technique can effectively supplement the judgement of on-site operators and raise confidence in the process as a whole.
park2026shape: Interest in 3D shape recognition has grown with recent advances in artificial intelligence. Aiming at automated shape recognition from CAD data in the manufacture of aircraft parts, this study uses SsdNet, a model with excellent recognition capability for deep-learning-based object detection, and analyses medium-to-large materials of 3 m or more rather than the standard shapes of the earlier first study. Recognition performance was optimised by applying pre-processing techniques such as voxel conversion and overlapping segmentation. The experiments achieved an average recognition accuracy of 83.3% over eight shapes, although the recognition rate fell for complex shapes involving curved structures and overlap, confirming that further research is needed to overcome these limitations. The study is expected to contribute to improving the productivity of aircraft part machining through automated shape recognition in NC (Numerical Control) programming in future smart manufacturing environments.
lee2024safety: With the recent trend toward urban air mobility, aircraft are becoming smaller and turning into software-intensive systems. Safety analysis techniques and standards centred on ARP4761, the aircraft safety assessment process, therefore need to change so that they too centre on software. This paper links the STPA method with the FTA and FMEA safety analysis techniques in order to analyse the safety of air mobility as a software-intensive system. To establish how far STPA, FTA and FMEA can be linked and to what effect, a safety analysis case study was carried out on collision avoidance software for a small aircraft. Through the proposed method and the case analysis, the paper confirms the effect of linking the STPA, FTA and FMEA safety techniques and elicits safety requirements.
park2024shape: For a long time, NC (Numerical Control) engineers have performed hundreds of similar operations by hand for NC programming, working from the three-dimensional design information produced by the design department, in order to machine parts on the manufacturing line. This paper reports a first attempt at experimenting with object detection technology that recognises the shapes of major aircraft parts. A meaningful accuracy of 93% on average was obtained for seven of the nine shapes, and after the tests the causes were investigated for the features that went unrecognised. Finally, the study acquired the base knowledge needed for recognising the shape of large bulkheads made up of aircraft structures. The results are expected to be used in automating NC programming for the machining of aircraft parts.
lim2022failsafe: The existing method of eliciting fail-safe design requirements for domestically developed rotorcraft systems can, when applied to modern integrated avionics systems, miss the factors by which the failure of a single item causes a critical system function failure. The cause is that the fail-safe design targets are selected on the basis of the effect a single item's failure has on system function. To resolve this, the present study draws on the functional hazard assessment and development assurance level allocation procedures of SAE ARP4754A, the international standard for civil aircraft development, and presents a systematic analysis procedure for eliciting fail-safe design requirements for a system architecture. To confirm that the presented procedure resolves the problem described above, cross-validation was performed by assuming a system architecture containing a single factor capable of causing a critical function failure. As a result, critical common causes that the existing method had missed could be identified, and fail-safe design requirements for controlling them were shown to be elicited.
park2021multilabel: The GitHub platform, which many developers use when developing open-source software, provides an issue management system. Using it, those involved can report a problem in the software or a functional request as an issue. GitHub's issue management system lets developers freely create labels on issue reports so as to classify issues. Because labelling is done by hand, however, it takes considerable effort and inaccurate labelling can easily occur; and reading unlabelled issues one by one in order to give feedback takes a great deal of time. Studies exist that attach a single label in order to address these problems. In real issue reports, however, there are a good number of issues that need several labels attached. This study therefore proposes a multi-labelling bot that automatically attaches multiple labels, so as to reduce the effort GitHub project managers spend reading issue reports and giving feedback. The multi-label classification technique used in the proposed bot showed an accuracy of 0.54 and an F1 score of 0.78.
bae2020rnn: A system that recommends the files a developer needs to change reduces the developer's working time. Such recommendation systems, however, generally take a long time to train on accumulated data, and they spend a great deal of time retraining every time new data accumulates. This study proposes a method of reducing training time in a code change recommendation system based on a recurrent neural network (RNN-CRS) by avoiding unnecessary training when new data has accumulated and the model has to be trained again. In an experimental evaluation across the five products used in the experiment, the proposed method reduced the time taken to regenerate the learning model after new data accumulated by 49.08%-68.15% compared with previous work where the saving was large, and by 10.66% where it was small.

park2019methodcalls: To reduce the effort developers spend updating client software, previous studies have presented techniques that derive change rules by analysing the differences between release versions of a framework. Those studies, however, only generate change rules; they do not update the client system itself. To go beyond that limitation, this study presents a technique that automatically updates the method calls present in a client by making use of the change rules generated by an existing rule-generation tool. The technique was also implemented as a tool, and by experimenting with the automatic updating of method calls the study evaluates how well the extracted information was applied. In the evaluation, 279 of 547 method calls were updated automatically, and only two compilation errors were observed. This study contributes to research on reducing the effort client developers spend updating method calls as a framework's methods change.
sim2018classdiagram: Research on software visualisation matters because it can help developers understand a software system and carry out code changes. Recently presented bottom-up software visualisation tools are demonstrating that they can help developers in their work, with the advantage of showing only the code information the developer is actually working on. These tools have the weakness, however, of showing only the code the developer has explored. To assist code exploration by supplying related code information in a bottom-up visualisation tool, this paper presents a tool that shows the revision history of software as a class diagram. By showing the code information developers have committed as a class diagram in a single click, the presented tool helps developers understand code changes quickly. Through a case study, the paper also shows that the tool can be useful when developers carry out continuous change work over several days.
